intro: Tehillim (Psalms), the songs of King David, have carried Jewish prayers for three thousand years. When someone is sick, when a baby is on the way, on a yahrzeit or a birthday, Jews everywhere open the book of Tehillim. Here are the chapters customarily said for each occasion. Say them in Hebrew or in your own language: G-d hears every heart. And give some charity (tzedakah) in the merit of the person you are praying for.

situations.title: For someone who is sick
situations.text: Chapters customarily said for a refuah shleimah, a complete recovery. Add the sections of Psalm 119 that spell the person's Hebrew name, then the letters of the words kra satan (קרע שטן). Mention the person by their Hebrew name and their mother's Hebrew name.

situations.title: Pregnancy and a healthy birth
situations.text: Chapters customarily said during pregnancy for an easy, healthy birth. Psalm 20 is said especially when labor begins.
situations.dedication: For an easy and healthy birth for {name}

situations.title: Thanks for a new baby
situations.text: Give thanks for a healthy baby and mother with the song of thanksgiving and the blessing for children.
situations.dedication: In honor of the birth of {name}

situations.title: Yahrzeit and remembering a loved one
situations.text: Said on a yahrzeit, at the cemetery, or anytime in memory of a loved one. Add the sections of Psalm 119 that spell the person's Hebrew name and then the word neshamah (נשמה), soul.

situations.title: In a house of mourning (shiva)
situations.text: Psalm 49 is said after the prayers in a shiva house, for the elevation of the soul.

situations.title: Your birthday chapter
situations.text: On your birthday, begin saying the chapter that matches your new year of life: turning 40, you begin chapter 41, and say it every day all year. The Lubavitcher Rebbe encouraged everyone to keep this custom. Find your chapter below.

situations.title: Finding a match (shidduch)
situations.text: Chapters customarily said by, or for, someone hoping to find their soulmate.

situations.title: Travel and safety
situations.text: Said before a journey, together with the Traveler's Prayer (Tefilat HaDerech).

situations.title: Livelihood (parnassah)
situations.text: The Shepherd's psalm, a prayer of trust that G-d provides.

situations.title: For Israel and the Jewish people in hard times
situations.text: Chapters said by Jewish communities around the world for the safety of Israel and the Jewish people.
situations.dedication: For the safety of the people of Israel

situations.title: Giving thanks
situations.text: After a recovery, a safe journey or any kindness from Above.
